strategies.overview: By virtue of its access to the rare Extreme Speed paired with Swords Dance and a decent offensive typing, Lucario carves out a small niche as a setup sweeper that can revenge kill faster threats like Mienshao and Maushold. Its ample coverage also makes it difficult for defensive staples like Jirachi and Slowbro to handle it reliably. However, Lucario's poor bulk and mediocre initial power make it difficult to find setup opportunities, especially if it forgoes Air Balloon for Life Orb's extra power. It also struggles with an awkward Speed tier, causing it to rely heavily on Extreme Speed; as such, faster Ghost-types like Gengar and Mimikyu are able to revenge kill it with ease. Lucario also faces competition from other physical setup sweepers, especially those that have priority; Mimikyu has a better typing and defensive utility with Disguise, while Bisharp has superior bulk and power.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Lucario's solid Special Attack and wide special movepool makes a Nasty Plot set with Vacuum Wave a usable option. However, it faces stiff competition from other special setup sweepers, like Mew and Armarouge, while the lacking power of Vacuum Wave makes it less effective at revenge killing. A Choice Band set can be used for more immediate power while letting Lucario fit an extra attacking move. Justified can be used over Inner Focus in order to punish Knock Off from the likes of Cyclizar and Krookodile. Bullet Punch is significantly weaker than Extreme Speed but lets Lucario revenge kill Ghost-types like Mimikyu and Gengar, though both need to have been worn down to be KOed by the move.

Checks and Counters

Ground-types: Gastrodon and Gligar have the bulk to take even a boosted hit from Lucario before retaliating with a super-effective STAB Move or, in the case of Hippowdon, force it out with Whirlwind. Quagsire is also able to completely ignore Lucario's Swords Dance boosts and KO it with Earthquake, though it is completely walled if Lucario's Air Balloon is intact.

Ghost-types: Gengar and Mimikyu are immune to Extreme Speed and naturally outspeed Lucario, letting them revenge kill it with their powerful attacks. Basculegion-F walls non-Crunch variants and can run Choice Scarf to outspeed and revenge kill Lucario. Additionally, Tera Ghost from defensive Pokemon like Registeel can prevent Lucario from sweeping.

Physically Bulky Pokemon: If running Meteor Mash, Lucario is completely walled by Slowbro, which can cripple it with Thunder Wave or Scald burns. Chesnaught is able to take even a boosted Close Combat from Lucario before KOing it with Body Press.

Status: Talonflame can survive a non-Tera Normal Extreme Speed and punish Lucario with either Will-O-Wisp or Flame Body. Paralysis from Jirachi's Body Slam as well as Thunder Wave from the likes of Cresselia and Slowbro can also annoy Lucario, forcing it to rely more on Extreme Speed.

Chip Damage: Lucario is prone to being worn down by a combination of Life Orb recoil, Spikes, and Rocky Helmet held by defensive Pokemon like Gastrodon, Slowbro, and Hippowdon. When combined with its poor bulk, the residual damage leaves Lucario vulnerable to being picked off by even defensive Pokemon like Amoonguss and Cresselia.

movesets.name: Swords Dance
movesets.description:
Set Details

Lucario's access to the elusive combination of Swords Dance and Extreme Speed makes it a terrifying sweeper and revenge killer in the right circumstances. Meteor Mash serves as a powerful, if somewhat inaccurate, STAB move with the occasional Attack boost being a nice bonus that can further bolster Lucario's power. Crunch is a reliable coverage option that can be used to hit Psychic-types like Slowbro and Cresselia as well as Basculegion-F, which otherwise walls it. Life Orb further bolsters Lucario's power at the cost of gradually wearing it down throughout the game; after a Swords Dance, it enables Lucario to guarantee a OHKO on Jirachi and, with Stealth Rock or Spikes damage, Gastrodon with Close Combat as well as Nasty Plot Mew with Crunch after chip damage. Air Balloon can instead be used as a means to set up against Gastrodon and Krookodile lacking Close Combat, as well as completely wall Quagsire. It also provides Lucario temporary protection from Spikes and Sticky Web. Inner Focus is used to block Intimidate from Krookodile while also blocking flinches from Jirachi's Iron Head. Tera Normal bolsters Extreme Speed's power; with a Life Orb, this lets Lucario OHKO Noivern and, with chip damage or a Weak Armor activation, Armarouge with the move after a Swords Dance.

Lucario provides offensive structures, particularly hyper offense teams, with a potent revenge killer and setup sweeper. Other physically offensive threats, like Krookodile, Mimikyu, and Maushold, can help Lucario wear down shared checks like Gastrodon and Quagsire. Maushold in particular can remove entry hazards with Tidy Up, which is especially appreciated by Life Orb variants due to their tendency to get worn down. Life Orb Lucario also appreciates entry hazard setters with Taunt, such as Mew and Terrakion, as they can help wear down the opposing team with the entry hazards they set while preventing the opponent from getting hazards up. Lucario makes for a great partner with Armarouge due to its ability to take on the likes of Assault Vest Cyclizar, Hisuian Goodra, and Umbreon while also taking care of opposing priority users like Feraligatr with Extreme Speed. In return, Armarouge is able to exploit and eliminate physically defensive Pokemon like Slowbro and Registeel. Other specially offensive threats like Gardevoir and Gengar can dent and possibly cripple the physical walls that Lucario struggles with while also appreciating Lucario's ability to take care of opposing revenge killers.

Since then, this Pokemon's viability has massively dropped off, and it is no longer relevant. Using this Pokemon in today's metagame is not advised unless you have an extremely niche, hyper-specific need to cover.

movesets.name: Magic Guard
movesets.description: Lucario's niche lies in its great mixed wallbreaking capacity and amazing STAB combination, with Close Combat and Steel Beam hitting the majority of the metagame for good damage and potentially 2HKOing them. Earthquake deals with Toxapex, Dark Pulse smacks Gholdengo, and Stone Edge prevents Zapdos and Iron Moth from switching in safely. Nasty Plot lets it muscle through bulky teams that try to dance around its coverage moves. An alternative EV spread of 252 Atk / 4 SpA / 252 Spe can be used to deal more damage on the physical side. Lucario's excellent wallbreaking abilities make fast offensive partners like Roaring Moon, Deoxys-S, and Chien-Pao good partners, as they can clean up after it has broken holes into the opposing team. Lucario's lack of defensive utility makes walls like Corviknight, RegenVest Manaphy, and Swampert much appreciated; additionally, they can bring it back onto the field with a slow pivot. Lucario greatly struggles with four-moveslot syndrome, so teammates that can deal with Zapdos and Iron Moth like RegenVest or Magic Guard Roaring Moon when not using Stone Edge and teammates that can switch into Gholdengo like Swampert when not running Dark Pulse are appreciated.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 6 onwards

Price Range: 5-6 points

Overview: On paper, Lucario possesses many desirable traits for an offensive Pokemon such as strong setup options, diverse mixed coverage, and powerful priority that includes the coveted Extreme Speed, allowing it to be a potentially deadly cleaner late-game, especially if accentuated by Terastallization. In practice, however, its relatively unimpressive attacking stats and Speed often necessitate boosts for it to perform its role, which can be difficult to obtain with its high frailty. Additionally, Lucario can struggle to fit in all the moves it wants, whether its due to having a moveslot taken up by a setup move or needing too much coverage, meaning that in certain matchups it might be forced into choosing what it gets checked by.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Setup Sweeper: With any of its offense-boosting options, Lucario can break through most walls with its STAB moves and coverage while using priority to fend off faster offensive threats. These sets best take advantage of Terastallization by powering up Lucario's crucial priority moves or letting it smash through walls with greater ease.

Revenge Killer: Lucario's access to multiple forms of powerful priority allows it to pick off low-health foes before they can make another move.

Wallbreaker: Though Lucario is usually outclassed as a wallbreaker by other Pokemon, opponents can be caught off guard by an all-out offensive Lucario capable of punching holes in the enemy team for its teammates. These sets typically require one of the Choice items in order to best supplement Lucario's below-average offensive stats.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Close Combat, Meteor Mash, Focus Blast, Aura Sphere, Vacuum Wave, Flash Cannon, Bullet Punch

Setup Moves: Swords Dance, Nasty Plot, Calm Mind, Bulk Up, Agility, Trailblaze

Utility Moves: Substitute, Roar

Coverage: Extreme Speed, Crunch, Stone Edge, Ice Punch, Earthquake, Rock Slide, Thunder Punch, Zen Headbutt, Poison Jab, Shadow Claw, Dark Pulse, Psychic, Dragon Pulse, Shadow Ball

Niche Moves

Steel Beam: Being Lucario's highest possible damage output, Steel Beam should only be used in situations where Lucario needs an immediate burst of power, such as catching a physical wall off guard.

Upper Hand: While Lucario's Extreme Speed will usually beat out other forms of priority, Upper Hand can possibly negate an attempt to quickly dispatch Lucario for a turn, letting it survive and force the opponent into predicting its next move.

Common Items

Life Orb: Lucario's stats often leave it quite power hungry even with boosts, making Life Orb the best option to maximize its KO potential. Due to its frailty and reliance on priority moves, it will rarely suffer the drawbacks of recoil damage.

Focus Sash: Focus Sash lets Lucario have a guaranteed setup or attacking turn, getting around its frailty.

Choice Band: Choice Band gives Lucario immediate power to smash defensive pieces with its high-powered STAB moves while retaining its decent cleaning potential with Extreme Speed.

Niche Items

Other Damage-boosting Items: Items like Expert and Black Belt supplement Lucario's power without drawbacks, though with noticeably less potency than its primary options.

Choice Specs: In a similar vein to Choice Band, Choice Specs can let Lucario perform immediately with its slightly higher Special Attack.

Tera

While one should look for greater potential and flexibility in their secondary Tera Captain, Lucario can still decently complement a faster primary Tera Captain, since it does not necessarily rely on Terastallization to function but greatly benefits from it as an option. Tera Normal is the most standout choice for Lucario, as boosting its Extreme Speed lets it more easily pick off chipped offensive Pokemon and clean up late-game with setup. Tera Fighting and Steel also make Lucario's Close Combat, Meteor Mash, or other STAB moves extremely potent at breaking down even neutrally hit walls while also boosting some of the other priority moves it wants to use. Other types like Tera Dark, Ground, and Electric can boost coverage moves against Fighting-resistant targets.

Draft Strategy

Lucario serves as a supplemental offensive piece that primarily seeks to clean up weakened teams. However, it still heavily relies on assistance from Pokemon with other roles on the team to make the most out of its only decent offensive potential.

Higher-tiered Sweepers: Teammates like Darkrai, Ogerpon-W, and Zarude can soften the enemy team enough for Lucario to sufficiently pick off the remaining pieces with setup, or they can alternatively benefit from Lucario's lesser weakening of foes to set up themselves.

Slow Pivots: Lucario appreciates being brought in by Pokemon like Galarian Slowking, Alomomola, and Primarina so that it does not have to rely on a KOed teammate for reliable entry.

Entry Hazard Control: Entry hazard setters like Gliscor and Mew make it easier for Lucario to achieve KOs against chipped foes. Since Lucario dislikes running Heavy-Duty Boots, teammates like Terapagos and Iron Treads can let it stay healthy without choosing between having its already subpar bulk being dug into or giving up its item.

Checks and Counters

Faster Offensive Foes: Without setup or a good amount of prior damage, faster Pokemon like Deoxys-S, Cinderace, and Garchomp can easily prey upon Lucario's low bulk without fearing a KO from its priority.

Fighting-resistant Walls: Lucario relies on its strong Fighting-type STAB moves to power through defensive pieces, but its somewhat weak coverage means that walls like Zapdos, Pecharunt, and Uxie can usually stomach even its boosted attacks to fire a decent hit back. If multiple of such Pokemon are present on the enemy team, Lucario's moveset can become extremely strained to the point of unfavorable moveslot compromises.

Residual Damage: Factors like Life Orb recoil, entry hazard damage, and Rocky Helmet contact can greatly lessen Lucario's longevity, making it susceptible to even attacks from weaker walls.
